Only what differs from the defaults — which is
          exactly the shape of a built-in preset, so one you like here pastes
          straight in as one. save as… keeps it in this browser;
          the json is what travels, between machines and between the builder
          and a player.

Cell scale and spoke count re-tessellate rather than
        slide, so the field boils on the way across. MIDI CC 11 drives
        this slider.

      

        
        
      

      

      
The player is what most people get: these presets and
        nothing else. publish player writes a standalone page with the
        set and its presets baked in, so it does not depend on what is in
        anyone's browser storage.

    


    

      
Background — gradient

      

        
        
        
        
        
      

      
      

        
      

      
This is what gets refracted through the glass.
        Drop a file anywhere on the page. The front camera is mirrored, the
        rear one is not — mirror source in the panel overrides that.
        Then hit record to capture the cracking over the live camera;
        camera and recording both need the downloaded fracture.html
        (or a permitted origin), not the embedded preview.

    


    

      
Seed — same as background

      

        
        
      

      

        
      

      
      
      
Luminance drives the fracture: fine dicing inside the
        bright areas, a wandering crack on the boundary, impact webs outside.
        Turn on seeded mode below.

    Audio needs mic permission — it listens for spectral-flux
        onsets. MIDI note-on maps pitch → position, velocity → force.
    
    
    

    
    
      
    Tilt — glass thickness
    
      
    
        
        
        
        
      
    
      
    
        
        
        
      
    
      
    The plate has two surfaces. Tilting shifts what you see
        through it and opens up the cut inner edge of every hole.
        device needs motion permission and a real sensor;
        pointer and auto work anywhere. In Resolume there is no
        sensor — drive tilt x/y from MIDI or audio instead.
    
    
    

    
    
      
    Sound
    
      
    
        
        
      
    
      
    The instrument is a DOCUMENT, not a mixer snapshot:
        which voices play, how loud, what kind of room, which scale. It saves
        as json, it can be pasted between machines, and a preset can point at
        one — referenced, never owned, the same as the word scripts. A set
        written for another instrument loads here, plays with the parts this
        engine knows, and keeps the rest when you save it.
    
    
    

    
    

    
    
      
    Output
    

      
    
        
        
        
      
    

    
    
      
    share
    
      
    
    
    
    
    
      
    
        
        
        
      
    
      
    
        
        
      
    
      
    cast sends the glass — picture and instrument — to
        a screen on the same wifi over WebRTC, so the phone in your hand is not
        on the end of an HDMI cable. What leaves is the CANVAS, not the device:
        no status bar, no panel, no notification sliding across the work. The
        receiver is receive.html open in any browser; v opens the
        sheet that sets it up.
    
      
    png seq renders a numbered PNG sequence off its
        own clock — frame k is always frame k, whatever
        the machine is doing — and zips it. Set alpha output
        (top of the panel) to overlay first and the frames carry
        coverage in the alpha channel, ready to drop onto footage. An overlay
        brings the breakage, not the refraction: lensing needs a background to
        bend, and a flat RGBA layer has none.
    
      
    On the hosted page every save asks you to
        confirm first, and on iOS it opens the share sheet — which is where
        Save Image lives. Camera, mic and MIDI still need the
        downloaded fracture.html or a permitted origin.
    
      
    .fs exports the current settings as an ISF shader.
        Arena will not load it directly — paste it into an ISF node in Resolume
        Wire, set the patch category, compile to .cwired. For real
        background refraction the patch has to be a Mixer (blend mode)
        or sit on a Group layer.
